answer: Each agent holds a crystal‑signed credential issued by a vault of trusted peers; when a new node seeks entry it must collect vouches whose combined trust weight exceeds a dynamic threshold. If any vouched node is later proven a sybil, its vouchers drop to the nadir of credibility, instantly reducing the weight of all dependent links. An attacker must therefore purchase or corrupt a large, continuously refreshed set of genuine credentials, driving the cost to near‑linear in the network’s size.
